name: Free school foundation
note: Pay for a school that takes pupils whose families cannot: teachers, books and a midday meal from a land endowment, on the model of the alimenta and of every later charity school. It adds to the flow of schooling the school already gives, so it raises literacy faster; a further foundation in another town is another unit, dearer each time, and only as many can be filled as the literate can spare.
_internal: Upkeep is derived, not a price: annual staff hours at the wage book plus annual consumables at the price book plus a maintenance share of the build cost. Annual staff hours: {"scholar": 25000, "scribe": 5000}. Annual consumables: {"parchment_sheet": 2000, "wheat_kg": 60000}. Sizes of the foundation and every number under mechanics are temporary_heuristic values (CLAUDE.md 4.4); revenue is 0 because a benefaction sells nothing.

capability.lost_benefit: The free pupils it teaches and the standing it earns

name: Aqueduct, baths and sewers for a town
note: A town's water supply given as a gift: the channel, the pipes, public baths that heat it, and the sewer that takes it away. It needs crews to keep it clear every year or it silts and leaks. It lowers the loss of your people to the water-borne diseases; the next town is another unit.

Annual staff hours: {"labourer": 6000, "mason": 2000, "plumber": 2000}. Annual consumables: {"charcoal_kg": 50000}. Sizes of the foundation and every number under mechanics are temporary_heuristic values (CLAUDE.md 4.4); revenue is 0 because a benefaction sells nothing. name: Harbour works and lighthouse
note: A breakwater, quays and a fire on a tower. Ships that can shelter and find the mouth at night arrive; those that arrive bring buyers, so it widens the market you can reach and spares some losses at sea. The fire burns charcoal and the moles need dredging for as long as the harbour is kept.
_internal: Upkeep is derived, not a price: annual staff hours at the wage book plus annual consumables at the price book plus a maintenance share of the build cost. Annual staff hours: {"labourer": 4000, "mason": 1500, "sailor": 3000}. Annual consumables: {"charcoal_kg": 100000, "olive_oil_kg": 5000}. Sizes of the foundation and every number under mechanics are temporary_heuristic values (CLAUDE.md 4.4); revenue is 0 because a benefaction sells nothing. [GATE: Built into a harbour that is kept up: breakwater and quay shelter it, and a drydock basin or a lighthouse serves a port that exists.]

capability.lost_benefit: The wider market a safe harbour opens and the ships it spares

name: Endowed free press
note: Money to keep a paper printing whether or not it sells: printers, correspondents, engravers and a stock of paper and ink, with the news and the prices of distant markets in every issue. It teaches the town to read by giving it something to read, it widens the markets you can sell to, and it earns a name. A paper that prints what officials would rather not read draws their eye to your work and to you. More papers in more towns are further units.
_internal: Upkeep is derived, not a price: annual staff hours at the wage book plus annual consumables at the price book plus a maintenance share of the build cost. Annual staff hours: {"artisan": 8000, "engraver": 3000, "scribe": 12000}. Annual consumables: {"ink_kg": 800, "paper_kg": 8000}. Sizes of the work and every number under mechanics are temporary_heuristic values (CLAUDE.md 4.4); revenue is 0 because a benefaction sells nothing. The alarm and eminence factors are labelled heuristics; the alarm factor multiplies the alarm of every project while the press is open because the engine has no per-state legitimacy or public opinion field. The prerequisite prn_newspaper_institution already carries the status_threatening trait and a negative government stance.

name: Electric lighting for a city
note: Arc and filament lamps along a town's streets and squares, with the lamplighters' replacement: electricians to keep the lines and lamps, glass and copper to renew them. It draws power from the grid the whole time it is lit. Lit streets are safer for the people you employ after dark, lend your name a little respect, and discourage the thieves who work in the dark. The next town is another unit.
_internal: Upkeep is derived, not a price: annual staff hours at the wage book plus annual consumables at the price book plus a maintenance share of the build cost. Annual staff hours: {"electrician": 9000, "labourer": 3000}. Annual consumables: {"copper_kg": 300, "glass_raw_kg": 800}. Sizes of the work and every number under mechanics are temporary_heuristic values (CLAUDE.md 4.4); revenue is 0 because a benefaction sells nothing. Engine readers checked: hazard_counters in HAZARD_COUNTERS (staff_loss), protection in update_protection, standing in standing_floor. No electricity_gate is declared here: the node's prerequisites already lead through power_grid, which the electricity load scan (_electricity_load_node_ids) treats as needing generated electricity, so the open works draws the standing electric load without a second declaration. The shares are labelled heuristics. The working-day and light-demand effects of street lighting have no field and are not modelled.

capability.lost_benefit: The lit streets and the safety and standing they bring

name: Fortified trading post
note: A walled depot on a far coast with a storehouse, a landing, a garrison of labourers and a factor with clerks. Ships put in to refit, trade and take on stores, so goods travel further and fewer voyages are lost. It is not a colony: it holds no land beyond its walls and no people but its own, and it is kept up at your cost every year. Another post on another coast is a further unit.
